text: When you're using Microsoft 365 Co-Pilot, a lot of your work contacts may already exist. With WorkIQ, Co-Pilot can use information you already have permission to access across services like Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and other 365 apps. Co-Pilot connectors can then extend that context to additional business systems. In Microsoft 365 Co-Pilot, what Co-Pilot can access depends on your license, your permissions, but also your organization's admin settings. You can find work contacts by opening up a Co-Pilot chat, making sure that WorkIQ is turned on, and then select the plus button to choose data sources. Here you can see and control the work sources available to Co-Pilot, and this can differ by chat. To manage external sources, you can go to settings and then sources, and you may also see information about your work contacts under settings, personalization, and then work profile. So for this demo, I'm going to use Microsoft 365 Co-Pilot to prepare for an upcoming meeting. So first of all, I'm going to make sure that WorkIQ is turned on here, and now with WorkIQ enabled, Co-Pilot can use the work information I already have permission to access like emails and meetings and team conversations and files, but I can also select plus, change data sources to see and choose which sources will be available. So now I can ask, hey, help me prepare for my meeting with Acme tomorrow. Find the relevant meeting details, recent emails, team conversations, and documents and summarize what I need to know. So instead of me manually searching Outlook, Team SharePoint, etc., Co-Pilot can bring together relevant information from across my Microsoft 365 environment. Now, of course, I still want to verify the results, so I'm going to review the citations and check that Co-Pilot found the correct meeting, the latest conversations, and the relevant files. This is crucial. Okay, now let's talk about connecting external work sources, because of course, not all work lives inside Microsoft 365. You may be using systems like Salesforce or Jira or ServiceNow, and this is exactly where Co-Pilot connectors come in. You can go to settings and enter sources to see which external sources you can connect or manage. A connector expands the context that Co-Pilot can work with by giving it access to information from additional systems. What appears here, of course, depends on what your organization has enabled and what you have permission to access. Now, a couple of practical notes to wrap up this section. At first of all, WorkIQ does not give you any new permissions, so you only have access to what you already have access to on your account. The available data and connectors, again, they vary by license, permissions, and by admin settings. Your administrator also may need to enable external connectors, and again, you always want to review the sources that Co-Pilot uses for important work.
